title: Search in Start or the taskbar finds nothing or shows no web results
tip: Search settings and the Bing Search app control what the search box can show. Reverting the newest one first is the quickest test.

title: Notifications stopped showing, or apps do not run in the background
tip: Notification and background app permissions are machine wide or per account. An app that cannot run in the background cannot notify you either.

title: The camera or microphone does not work in an app
tip: Camera and microphone permissions are checked before the app sees the device. Also look at Windows privacy settings for the app itself.

title: Bluetooth or Wi-Fi devices will not connect or pair
tip: Radio and device permissions decide which apps can control Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. A driver problem looks the same, so check Device Manager too.

title: Websites will not load or show DNS errors
tip: A DNS provider that is blocked on your network, or encrypted DNS that a router or filter does not allow, breaks lookups. Reverting restores the servers you had before.

title: Game Bar, game clips or Xbox features stopped working
tip: Game recording settings and the Xbox apps are separate. Reverting the recording settings brings clips back, and removed apps come back from Revert or the Microsoft Store.

title: An app I used is gone
tip: Revert restores it if Windows still has the files, otherwise reinstall it from the Microsoft Store.

title: Clipboard history, sync between PCs or Find my device stopped working
tip: Sync and clipboard settings switch these features off for the account or the whole PC. Sign-in information permissions can also affect them.

title: The PC sleeps, wakes or starts up differently, or battery life changed
tip: Power plans, hibernation and fast startup change how the PC sleeps and boots. Reverting the newest one shows whether it is the cause.

title: Windows Update waits, skips drivers or does not restart when I expect
tip: Clarion never turns Windows Update off. These settings only delay feature updates, skip driver updates or stop automatic restarts.

title: The right click menu, taskbar or File Explorer looks or behaves differently
tip: These only change how Windows looks and where things are. They are safe to revert one at a time.

title: The mouse or keyboard feels different
tip: Pointer acceleration, menu delay and sticky keys settings change how input feels. Revert to get the Windows defaults back.

title: Voice typing, speech recognition or typing suggestions stopped working
tip: Online speech and typing personalization settings turn off cloud features. Voice typing and dictation need online speech to be allowed.

title: Edge starts slower or has lost its sidebar, shopping or personalization
tip: Edge policies change what Edge does at startup and in the browser. Reverting removes the policy value.

title: Weather, maps, time zone or other location features stopped working
tip: Turning location off for apps stops anything that needs to know where the PC is.

title: An optional Windows feature is missing (WSL, Hyper-V, Sandbox, older games or .NET)
tip: Windows features can be turned on and off here. Reverting puts the feature back, and Windows may need a restart to finish.

title: I cannot reach an old network drive, NAS or remote help session
tip: Turning off the old SMB1 protocol blocks very old devices on purpose. Remote assistance and network file sharing features are separate switches.

title: Inserting a USB drive or disc does nothing
tip: Autoplay is off, so Windows no longer opens a prompt. The drive still shows up in File Explorer.

title: Copilot, Recall or Paint AI tools are missing
tip: These settings hide or turn off the AI features on purpose. Reverting brings them back where your Windows edition has them.

title: An app says it cannot read my contacts, calendar, email, messages or call history
tip: These permissions decide whether apps can read that information. Turning them off blocks the app, not just tracking.

title: A fitness, motion, eye tracking or presence feature stopped working
tip: Motion, eye tracker and presence permissions block apps from reading those sensors. Devices that dim or lock when you leave use presence.

title: The lock screen shows less than it did
tip: Lock screen settings control the camera shortcut, app notifications and tips. Reverting restores them.

title: Start, jump lists or Quick access no longer show recent files, folders or most used apps
tip: Recent item and app launch tracking are off, so those lists stay empty or short. Reverting lets Windows build them up again.
